headline: Committee recommends passing bill creating H3 and H4 districts, 6–1

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.summary: The committee voted six to one, with two members excused, to recommend passage. An amendment leaving Molokaʻi out of the new districts passed earlier. The bill now goes to the full council.
meeting.recap: Planning staff said the new districts copy the A1 and A2 apartment district rules and do not rezone any property now.[[0:08:54]] All three planning commissions recommended denial of the bill.[[0:10:27]] A Lahaina Strong representative testified against the new zoning.[[0:37:28]] Another testifier said he supports the bill only if properties have security, housekeeping, a front desk and staff on site.[[1:38:34]] A member moved to limit the new districts to properties that already met the rules for vacation rentals in apartment districts.[[3:30:19]] A second amendment leaves Molokaʻi out of the new districts, as the Molokaʻi Planning Commission asked.[[3:52:36]] That amendment passed with seven ayes and no noes.[[3:55:13]] The committee voted six to one, with two members excused, to recommend passing the bill.[[4:26:19]] The bill now goes to the full council.[[4:27:02]]
meeting.next: The bill moves on to the full council for its consideration. Planning staff said moving specific properties into H3 or H4 would be a separate, second step.

moments.q: Planning staff correct a side setback in the bill to 15 feet, not 20
